before.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

before.claim: 1.1 (Almost-everywhere cone inequality.) Write $c(t):=x(\gamma(t))=(c^0(t),c_s(t))$. By [L1], $c$ is locally absolutely continuous and at almost every $t$ its derivative $c'(t)$ exists and equals the coordinates of the nonzero future causal velocity, so by [L2] $c^0{}'(t)\ge|c_s'(t)|_{\mathrm e}$ and $c^0{}'(t)>0$. This proves nothing yet but fixes the a.e. information used below.

2.1 (Monotonicity and the Lipschitz bound.) Let $a<b$ in $I$. By [L3] applied to the absolutely continuous functions $c^0$ and the components of $c_s$ on $[a,b]$, and by [L4], $$c^0(b)-c^0(a)=\int_a^bc^0{}'\ge\int_a^b|c_s'|_{\mathrm e}\ge\bigl|c_s(b)-c_s(a)\bigr|_{\mathrm e}\ge0 .$$ This is (b). If $c^0(b)=c^0(a)$, then $\int_a^bc^0{}'=0$ with $c^0{}'\ge0$ almost everywhere, so [L4] gives $c^0{}'=0$ almost everywhere on $[a,b]$, contradicting $c^0{}'>0$ on the full-measure set of step 1.1; hence $c^0(b)>c^0(a)$, which is the strict monotonicity of (a). Moreover $c(a)=c(b)$ would give $c_s(a)=c_s(b)$ by the displayed inequality, hence $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$, and strict increase of $c^0$ forbids $a<b$; so $\gamma$ is injective, and its spatial coordinates are $1$-Lipschitz in $c^0$ again by the displayed inequality.

3.1 (Unboundedness at inextendible ends.) Suppose $\gamma$ is future-inextendible and let $T:=\sup\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)$. If $T<+\infty$, then for $t,t'\to\sup I$ the spatial coordinates satisfy $|c_s(t)-c_s(t')|_{\mathrm e}\le|c^0(t)-c^0(t')|\to0$ by step 2.1, so $(c^0,c_s)$ has a limit $q=(T,z_\infty)\in\mathbb R^4$; that is, $\gamma$ converges to the event with coordinates $q$ as $t\to\sup I$. By [L5] this makes $\gamma$ extendible at its upper end, contradicting future-inextendibility. Hence $T=+\infty$; the past statement is the time reverse. With both statements, an inextendible $\gamma$ has range all of $\mathbb R$, and step 2.1 makes $x^0\circ\gamma$ a strictly increasing surjection onto $\mathbb R$, so each level set is attained at exactly one parameter. This proves (c).

4.1 (The time coordinate is temporal, and conclusion.) In the coordinates of the global inertial chart, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the vector field $w:=-\partial_0$ satisfies $\eta(w,\partial_0)=1$ and $\eta(w,\partial_i)=0$ for $i=1,2,3$; hence $\eta(w,X)=X^0=du(X)$ for every vector $X$, so $w$ is the gradient $\nabla u$ of $u=x^0$. It satisfies $\eta(w,w)=-1<0$ and $du(\partial_0)=1>0$, so $u$ is a temporal function as claimed in (d). With steps 2.1 and 3.1 this completes the proof.
